faqs.q: Sec. 2-371. - Purpose and declaration of policy.
faqs.a:
The proper operation of democratic government requires that public officers be independent,
               impartial and responsible to the people; that government decisions and policy be made
               within the proper channels of the governmental structure; that public office not be
               used for personal gains; and that the public have confidence in the integrity of its
               government. In recognition of these goals, these rules of behavior and standards of
               conduct for all city officers is hereby adopted. The purpose of the rules of behavior
               and standards of conduct is to establish guidelines for ethical standards of conduct
               for all such officers by setting forth those acts or actions that are incompatible
               with the best interest of the city and by directing disclosure by such officers of
               private financial or other interests in matters affecting the city. By eliminating
               conflicts of interest and providing a guide for conduct in city matters, the city
               council hopes to promote the faith and confidence of the citizens in their government.
               The holding of public officer is a public trust created by the confidence which the
               electorate reposes in the integrity of public officers. Public officers serve their
               government in a fiduciary capacity and must not bestow special consideration upon
               any person or group but carry out their official duties for the benefit of all people
               of the city. Officers have sworn an oath to uphold the Constitution of the United
               States, state and the ordinances of the city. Furthermore, the citizens of the city
               have adopted the principles of the council-manager form of city government and to
               that end have declared that the principles of that form of government require that
               the city manager administer the administrative functions of the city subject to the
               city council's directions, free from individual councilmember's interference in the
               day-to-day administrative operations of the city. The citizens of the city have reposed
               all policymaking and legislative power in the city council which shall act as a body.
               Except by city council delegation, no councilmember has any authority to exercise
               the power of their office except as set forth in the Charter and Code. The council-manager
               form of government also requires an informed council and therefore, it is consistent
               with the council-manager form of government for councilmembers to inquire of department
               heads as provided for in the Charter for the purpose of obtaining information. Finally,
               the purpose of this Code is to provide clear conduct guidelines and necessary enforcement
               procedures, and to fully implement the provisions of section
4.2.1
of the Charter.
(Code 1981, § 2-51; Ord. No. 3088, § 2, 6-27-1994)
